title: F172 - Lesson 10: Gene Therapy Clinical Trials & Task 2 Research (ANT-130)
courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology - Unit F172: Genetics
focus: Gene Therapy Clinical Trials & Task 2 Research: ANT-130 (AMT-130) Case Study, Biomarkers, and OCR Genetics NEA Marking Criteria
deliverable: OCR AAQ Level 3 Human Biology (Unit F172: Genetics) Lesson 10 presentation with embedded Assessment Points and Learner Activities: Starter 6-box retrieval grid, clinical trial phases (I-III), uniQure ANT-130 (AMT-130) AAV5-miRNA striatal microinfusion for Huntington's disease, CSF biomarker data workshop (mHTT and NfL), functional metrics (cUHDRS, TMS), genetic counselling consultation roleplay, and NEA Task 2 Distinction writing workshop (Pass P3-P8, Merit M2-M5, Distinction D1-D3).

objectives.knowledge: Explain clinical trial architecture (Phases I–III) and the molecular mechanism of ANT-130 (AAV5-miRNA targeting HTT mRNA via RNAi).
objectives.application: Interpret primary clinical trial data: dose-dependent CSF mHTT reduction, transient vs chronic Neurofilament Light (NfL) dynamics, and cUHDRS functional deceleration.
objectives.evaluation: Evaluate trial methodology (sham controls, small cohorts, irreversible intracranial surgery) and align coursework to Genetics NEA Task 2 Distinction criteria.

terminology.def: An investigational AAV5-miRNA gene therapy delivering microRNA directly into the caudate and putamen to silence toxic mutant huntingtin (mHTT) via RNA interference.
A sensitive biomarker of active neuroaxonal damage; initial post-operative spike followed by long-term decline below baseline indicates neuroprotection.
A multidimensional clinical rating score combining total motor score, total functional capacity, and cognitive measures to assess Huntington's disease progression.
OCR AAQ Level 3 coursework evaluating gene therapies against Pass (P5, P7, P8), Merit (M3, M4, M5), and Distinction (D3, D4, D5) criteria.

slides.title: Starter Retrieval Grid: Genetics & Gene Delivery Recall
slides.subtitle: Do Now Activity (5 Minutes) · Retrieve Prior Knowledge from Lessons 3–9
keyTakeaways: 1. HTT Mutation: CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion (>36 repeats) in exon 1 of HTT on chromosome 4.
2. AAV5 Tropism: High neuronal tropism and stable non-integrating episomal expression in post-mitotic neurons.
3. Delivery Routes: In vivo (systemic/local into patient), Ex vivo (cells modified in lab), In situ (direct into target structure).
4. Stereotactic CED: Positive-pressure microinfusion via intracranial cannulae directly bypasses endothelial tight junctions of the BBB.
5. miRNA Stage: Post-transcriptional gene silencing (translation stage) via RISC-mediated mRNA cleavage.
6. Autosomal Dominant Risk: 50% (1 in 2) probability of inheriting the mutant allele from a heterozygous parent.

reveals.question: 1. What trinucleotide repeat expansion on chromosome 4 causes Huntington's disease, and what is the pathological threshold?
reveals.expectedAnswer: CAG repeat expansion in exon 1 of the HTT gene on chromosome 4; pathological threshold is >36 CAG repeats (≥40 = full penetrance).

reveals.question: 2. Why is Adeno-Associated Virus serotype 5 (AAV5) selected for adult striatal neurons instead of a lentiviral vector?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Adult striatal neurons are post-mitotic (non-dividing); AAV5 has high CNS tropism and persists safely as non-integrating episomes without insertional mutagenesis risk.

reveals.question: 3. Distinguish between In Vivo, Ex Vivo, and In Situ gene therapy administration routes.
reveals.expectedAnswer: In Vivo: delivered into the body; Ex Vivo: patient cells modified outside the body & re-infused; In Situ: injected directly into the target anatomical tissue (e.g., striatum).

reveals.question: 4. How does stereotactic Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) overcome the Blood-Brain Barrier?
reveals.expectedAnswer: MRI-guided microcannulae bypass capillary tight junctions physically, using continuous positive-pressure bulk flow to distribute vectors evenly across the caudate and putamen.

reveals.question: 5. At which stage of gene expression (transcription vs translation) does microRNA (miRNA) gene silencing operate?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Post-transcriptional / Translation stage: miRNA loads into RISC to bind and cleave target mRNA transcripts before ribosomal translation into protein.

reveals.question: 6. Huntington's disease is autosomal dominant. What is the inheritance probability from a heterozygous affected parent?
reveals.expectedAnswer: 50% (1 in 2 or 0.5) probability for each child, regardless of sex, because a single copy of the expanded HTT allele is sufficient to cause the disorder.

slides.title: Huntington's Disease: Pathology & Genetic Architecture
slides.subtitle: Autosomal dominant CAG expansion, mHTT aggregation, and striatal degeneration

slides.title: Assessment Point 1: Molecular Pathology & RNAi Mechanism
slides.subtitle: Formative Checkpoint · OCR NEA Task 2 Pass Criteria (P3, P4, P6, P7) & Merit (M2)
keyTakeaways: Checkpoint 1 (P3/P4): >36 CAG repeats in HTT exon 1 -> expanded polyglutamine tract -> misfolded mHTT aggregates -> selective apoptosis of striatal GABAergic MSNs.
Checkpoint 2 (P6/P7): Tight junctions of the BBB block systemic AAV5; MRI-guided stereotactic CED delivers vectors directly into the caudate and putamen.
Checkpoint 3 (P6/M2): Pri-miHTT is processed by Dicer into mature miRNA, loaded into RISC, and binds exon 1 HTT mRNA for catalytic cleavage.
slides.text:
Assessment Point 1: Molecular Pathology & RNAi Mechanism
Formative Checkpoint · OCR NEA Task 2 Pass Criteria (P3, P4, P6, P7) & Merit (M2)
Checkpoint 1 (P3/P4): >36 CAG repeats in HTT exon 1 -> expanded polyglutamine tract -> misfolded mHTT aggregates -> selective apoptosis of striatal GABAergic MSNs.
Checkpoint 2 (P6/P7): Tight junctions of the BBB block systemic AAV5; MRI-guided stereotactic CED delivers vectors directly into the caudate and putamen.
Checkpoint 3 (P6/M2): Pri-miHTT is processed by Dicer into mature miRNA, loaded into RISC, and binds exon 1 HTT mRNA for catalytic cleavage.

reveals.question: Checkpoint 1 (Pathology Chain — P3/P4): Trace the pathogenic cascade from >36 CAG repeats in HTT exon 1 to MSN loss.
reveals.expectedAnswer: Model Answer (P3/P4 & M2): >36 CAG repeats in HTT exon 1 (Chr 4) translate into an expanded polyglutamine (polyQ) tract. Mutant huntingtin (mHTT) misfolds into toxic intracellular aggregates, causing selective apoptosis of GABAergic medium spiny neurons (MSNs) in the caudate and putamen, leading to chorea and cognitive decline.

reveals.question: Checkpoint 2 (Stereotactic CED — P6/P7): Justify why ANT-130 requires bilateral MRI-guided CED rather than IV injection.
reveals.expectedAnswer: Model Answer (P6/P7): The Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) blocks >98% of systemic viral vectors. Bilateral MRI-guided Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) places microcatheters directly into the caudate and putamen, using positive pressure to achieve homogeneous striatal transduction with a single surgical dose.

reveals.question: Checkpoint 3 (RNAi Silencing — P6/M2): Explain how Dicer and RISC enable miHTT to lower toxic mHTT protein.
reveals.expectedAnswer: Model Answer (P6/M2): Episomal AAV5 DNA transcribes artificial pri-miHTT, which is cleaved by cytoplasmic Dicer into mature microRNA and loaded into the RNA-Induced Silencing Complex (RISC). RISC binds complementary HTT mRNA and degrades it, preventing ribosomal translation of toxic mHTT.

slides.title: Learner Activity 1: Auditing NCT04120493 Trial Architecture
slides.subtitle: Paired Critical Thinking Task (8 Minutes) · Criteria M3 & D2
keyTakeaways: Task A: Combined Phase I/II design simultaneously tests surgical safety/dose escalation (Phase I) and biomarker target engagement (Phase II) in N=29 rare-disease patients.
Task B: Partial-thickness burr-hole sham surgery blinds patients and clinical raters, isolating true pharmacological efficacy from surgical placebo effects.
Task C: Unblinding sham controls at 12 months is ethically necessary so patients can cross over, but requires external propensity-matched natural history controls at 36 months.
slides.text:
Learner Activity 1: Auditing NCT04120493 Trial Architecture
Paired Critical Thinking Task (8 Minutes) · Criteria M3 & D2
Task A: Combined Phase I/II design simultaneously tests surgical safety/dose escalation (Phase I) and biomarker target engagement (Phase II) in N=29 rare-disease patients.
Task B: Partial-thickness burr-hole sham surgery blinds patients and clinical raters, isolating true pharmacological efficacy from surgical placebo effects.
Task C: Unblinding sham controls at 12 months is ethically necessary so patients can cross over, but requires external propensity-matched natural history controls at 36 months.

reveals.question: Task A (Phase I/II Classification): Why is NCT04120493 (N=29) a combined Phase I/II trial rather than Phase III?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Model Guidance: With N=29 (N=12 low-dose, N=17 high-dose), the trial combines Phase I acute neurosurgical safety & dose escalation with Phase II proof-of-concept biomarker tracking (CSF mHTT/NfL), whereas Phase III requires 100s of patients for definitive regulatory approval.

reveals.question: Task B (Sham Surgery Justification): Why did the control arm undergo superficial cranial bone drilling without dural penetration?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Model Guidance: Motor and functional scores (cUHDRS/TMS) are susceptible to patient and clinician expectation bias. Partial burr-hole imitation surgery maintains double-blinding without exposing control patients to intracranial catheter penetration risk.

reveals.question: Task C (Unblinding Critique — D2): How does unblinding sham controls after 12 months impact 36-month data validity?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Model Guidance (Distinction D2): Unblinding after 12 months removes the internal randomized placebo group for Years 2–3, forcing reliance on an external propensity score-matched natural history cohort (TRACK-HD/Enroll-HD), which may introduce residual confounding.

slides.title: Learner Activity 2: Interpreting CSF Biomarkers & cUHDRS Data
slides.subtitle: Data Analysis Workshop (10 Minutes) · Criteria M4, D1 & D2
keyTakeaways: Challenge 1: Post-op CSF NfL spike reflects physical microcannula insertion trauma; 36-month -8.2% drop below baseline demonstrates true neuroprotection.
Challenge 2: CSF mHTT is a molecular surrogate marker of target engagement, while cUHDRS (75% slowing, p=0.003) and TFC (60% slowing) measure real-world patient function.
Challenge 3: Propensity score-matched natural history comparisons provide strong Phase II evidence but require confirmatory randomized Phase III trials.
slides.text:
Learner Activity 2: Interpreting CSF Biomarkers & cUHDRS Data
Data Analysis Workshop (10 Minutes) · Criteria M4, D1 & D2
Challenge 1: Post-op CSF NfL spike reflects physical microcannula insertion trauma; 36-month -8.2% drop below baseline demonstrates true neuroprotection.
Challenge 2: CSF mHTT is a molecular surrogate marker of target engagement, while cUHDRS (75% slowing, p=0.003) and TFC (60% slowing) measure real-world patient function.
Challenge 3: Propensity score-matched natural history comparisons provide strong Phase II evidence but require confirmatory randomized Phase III trials.

reveals.question: Challenge 1 (The CSF NfL Curve): Why does CSF NfL spike acutely after surgery before dropping -8.2% below baseline at 36 months?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Data Key: Physical insertion of stereotactic catheters causes transient localized axonal disruption (acute NfL release). Once healed, AAV5-miHTT silences mHTT toxicity, slowing ongoing MSN neurodegeneration so NfL falls -8.2% below pre-treatment baseline by Month 36.

reveals.question: Challenge 2 (Surrogate vs Functional Endpoints): Contrast CSF mHTT lowering against cUHDRS (75% slowing) and TMS (59% slowing).
reveals.expectedAnswer: Data Key (D1/D2): Lowering CSF mHTT proves molecular target engagement, but does not automatically guarantee clinical recovery. Preserving cUHDRS (+75% slowing, p=0.003), TMS (+59%), and TFC (+60%) proves that mHTT knockdown translates into preserved motor and daily living independence.

reveals.question: Challenge 3 (Statistical vs Clinical Significance): Why does a propensity-matched natural history comparison require Phase III confirmation?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Data Key (D2/D3): Although p=0.003 shows strong statistical significance, the high-dose cohort is small (N=17) and compared against external natural history controls rather than a concurrent 36-month blinded placebo group. A larger Phase III RCT is required to confirm effect size.

slides.title: Evaluating Gene Therapy: Challenges & Delivery Risks
slides.subtitle: Surgical delivery risks, irreversibility, immune responses, and off-target effects
keyTakeaways: Invasive CED neurosurgery carries risks of intracranial hemorrhage, infection, and edema.
AAV5-miHTT delivery is irreversible ('no undo button') and non-selectively lowers wild-type HTT alongside mutant mHTT.

slides.title: Assessment Point 2: Evaluating Clinical & Molecular Risks
slides.subtitle: Diagnostic Risk-Benefit Evaluation · Criteria M3, M4 & D2
keyTakeaways: Prompt 1 (Irreversibility): Episomal AAV5 cassettes cannot be switched off or removed once infused into post-mitotic striatal neurons.
Prompt 2 (Wild-Type HTT): Wild-type huntingtin supports axonal transport and BDNF neurotrophic survival; excessive knockdown could impair neuronal health.
Prompt 3 (Immunity): Pre-existing anti-AAV5 neutralizing antibodies block vector transduction, while high capsid doses can trigger cytotoxic neuroinflammation.
slides.text:
Assessment Point 2: Evaluating Clinical & Molecular Risks
Diagnostic Risk-Benefit Evaluation · Criteria M3, M4 & D2
Prompt 1 (Irreversibility): Episomal AAV5 cassettes cannot be switched off or removed once infused into post-mitotic striatal neurons.
Prompt 2 (Wild-Type HTT): Wild-type huntingtin supports axonal transport and BDNF neurotrophic survival; excessive knockdown could impair neuronal health.
Prompt 3 (Immunity): Pre-existing anti-AAV5 neutralizing antibodies block vector transduction, while high capsid doses can trigger cytotoxic neuroinflammation.

reveals.question: Prompt 1 (Irreversible Delivery): Evaluate the clinical risk if delayed neurotoxicity emerges years post-infusion.
reveals.expectedAnswer: Model Evaluation (M3/D2): Because AAV5 episomes persist indefinitely in non-dividing neurons and constitutively express miHTT without an off-switch, treatment cannot be discontinued if late-onset off-target toxicity or excessive HTT depletion occurs.

reveals.question: Prompt 2 (Wild-Type HTT Depletion): Why must clinicians monitor long-term wild-type HTT knockdown?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Model Evaluation (M4/D2): Wild-type huntingtin protein is essential for vesicular transport, synaptic function, and BDNF transcription. Non-allele-specific silencing lowers both healthy and mutant HTT, requiring careful dosing so wild-type levels remain sufficient for cell survival.

reveals.question: Prompt 3 (Immunological Screening): Explain why pre-existing AAV5 antibodies or neuroinflammation compromise efficacy.
reveals.expectedAnswer: Model Evaluation (M3/M4): Neutralizing antibodies bind AAV5 capsids and prevent neuronal receptor attachment, while T-cell immune responses against viral capsid proteins can trigger striatal neuroinflammation, requiring perioperative immunosuppression.

slides.title: Patient Support: The Role of Genetic Counselling
slides.subtitle: Predictive presymptomatic testing, autosomal dominance, and patient autonomy
keyTakeaways: 50% inheritance risk requires pre-test counselling on psychological and family implications.
'The Right Not to Know' protects autonomy for asymptomatic individuals in affected pedigrees.
Counsellors manage expectations: ANT-130 stabilizes disease but cannot reverse lost brain tissue.

reveals.question: Consultation Task 1 (Autonomy & Testing — P8): How should the genetic counsellor advise Maya on predictive testing and reproductive options?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Counselling Protocol (P8): Explain her 50% autosomal dominant inheritance risk and that 44 CAG repeats carries 100% lifetime penetrance. Respect 'The Right Not to Know' (non-directive counselling), assess psychological readiness, and outline IVF with Pre-implantation Genetic Diagnosis (PGD) to have unaffected children.

reveals.question: Consultation Task 2 (Managing Expectations — M5): How should you explain ANT-130's realistic clinical benefit and trial consent?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Counselling Protocol (M5): Clarify that ANT-130 is a disease-modifying therapy that slows functional decline (75% cUHDRS slowing) by protecting surviving MSNs, NOT a regenerative cure for neurons already lost. Ensure informed consent covers irreversible brain surgery and the possibility of randomization to the sham surgical arm.

reveals.question: Step 1 (Evaluative Synthesis Draft — D2/D3): View Exemplar Distinction Evaluation Excerpt
reveals.expectedAnswer: Exemplar D2/D3 Excerpt: 'While high-dose ANT-130 demonstrated a 75% slowing on cUHDRS (p=0.003) and an 8.2% CSF NfL reduction at 36 months—indicating genuine striatal MSN preservation—these findings rely on a small cohort (N=29) compared against external natural history controls, and must be weighed against irreversible neurosurgery and non-selective wild-type HTT silencing.'

reveals.question: Step 2 (Three-Tier Peer Audit): View Pass / Merit / Distinction Audit Key
reveals.expectedAnswer: Audit Checklist: Pass = names CAG >36, AAV5-miHTT, CED & RISC; Merit = explains polyQ MSN toxicity, surgical hemorrhage/immune risks & pre-test counselling; Distinction = evaluates surrogate (mHTT/NfL) vs functional (cUHDRS) endpoints, critiques N=29 & unblinding, and justifies why one-time AAV5-miHTT remains the strongest disease-modifying candidate.

reveals.question: Step 3 (Harvard Academic Referencing): View Standard Harvard Reference Format
reveals.expectedAnswer: Harvard Citation Exemplar: In-text: (uniQure, 2024; Tabrizi et al., 2022). Reference List: uniQure (2024) Phase I/II clinical trial data of AMT-130 in Huntington's disease (NCT04120493): 24- and 36-month interim analysis. Amsterdam: uniQure N.V.
